Alger, 10 août 2026 (Algeria Tech) — La: Algiers, August 10, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — The Alouia Clinic performed the country's first robotic surgery operation, marking a major breakthrough for the Algerian healthcare system. Dr. Khelifa Aït Saït, who is spearheading the project, announced the creation of a national academy to train local professionals and reduce reliance on foreign countries.
Une première historique pour la santé al: A historic first for Algerian healthcare
Le Dr Aït Saïd ne s’arrête pas à cette p: Dr. Aït Saïd is not stopping at this initial success. He is driving an ambitious project: the creation of an Algerian academy for robotic surgery. This structure's mission will be to train not only surgeons, but also computer scientists, biomedical engineers, and cybersecurity specialists. The objective is clear: to make Algeria a regional training center and a digital health hub in Africa, while reducing dependence on foreign institutions.
Un projet structurant pour le système de: A structuring project for the healthcare system
Le projet s’articule autour d’un triptyq: The project is built around a triptych: "mastering the technology, transmitting expertise, and retaining skills within the country." Dr. Aït Saïd draws inspiration from international models, such as IRCAD in Strasbourg, a world reference in training for minimally invasive and robotic techniques. Beyond traditional training, he also envisions the development of telesurgery, enabling remote guidance of operations and democratizing access to high-level care throughout the country.
Former sur place plutôt qu’à l’étranger: Training locally rather than abroad is a strategic challenge for Algeria. The high cost of sending doctors abroad for training limits the number of beneficiaries and does not guarantee their return to the country. A local academy would multiply the number of professionals trained, adapt teaching to field realities, and anchor expertise locally. This approach is part of a broader African trend where several countries are seeking to reduce their dependence on European or North American institutions for ultra-specialized care.
Un écosystème complet autour de la chiru: A complete ecosystem surrounding robotic surgery
L’initiative du Dr Aït Saïd dépasse la s: Dr. Aït Saïd's initiative goes beyond the simple training of surgeons. It aims to create an integrated ecosystem surrounding research, education, clinical practice, and innovation. Several professionals will be involved:
Les chirurgiens pourront se former sur p: Surgeons will be able to train locally in a technology that is still rare on the continent, mastering precise and less invasive movements that improve patient prognoses.
Les médecins anesthésistes et radiologue: Anesthetists and radiologists will need to adapt their practices to closer coordination with medical imaging.
Les infirmiers de bloc opératoire seront: Operating room nurses will be trained in the specificities of robotic interventions.
Ce projet pourrait également stimuler l’: This project could also stimulate local innovation in the fields of medical robotics, biomedical equipment, and dedicated software solutions. Algeria could thus become a key player in digital health in Africa by combining medical expertise, training, and technological development.
